summary: Refund and bank-return first slice: within a server-derived refundable coverage (posted gross minus active clearance minus active refunds minus active bank returns) the owner/finance records a real reverse cash fact as a new posted CashTransaction (refund: direction=out from incoming cash; bank return: opposite of the original direction), plus an append-only Refund/BankReturn owned fact, generic audit, exactly one cash.refunded.v1 / cash.returned.v1 canonical event, and an idempotency receipt. The produced posted cash still goes through the PH-230 posting owner service, so every posted cash fact keeps its cash.transaction_recorded.v1 event and posting receipt. Coverage is symmetric: the settlement clearance write path and cash candidate availability now also subtract active refunds/returns, so cleared + refunded + returned can never exceed the posted gross. No accounting event, ledger posting, revenue, cost, receivable, payable, open item or clearance write; offset is reserved and explicitly not implemented; PH-239 later owns the cash book bridge for these new cash facts.

deviations: Reviewer round-1 blocker fixed: the worker-added 'cash namespace must not have a LedgerPosting' assertion was narrowed to refund/bank-return provenance only. It now rejects only AccountingEvents whose source kind is refund/bank_return or whose source points directly at a refund/return-produced cash fact (plus their postings), and explicitly allows the PH-243-frozen cash classification bridge (source kind cash_classification). A positive boundary regression creates classification-style bridge events (including one on a refund-produced cash fact) and asserts the refund guard does not fire, while a negative regression asserts refund-provenance ledger rows are rejected. Existing PH-230/PH-232 assertions were not touched; PH-239 replaces its own legacy blanket cash assertions.

Cross-owner write (Lead-approved option A): pmo_plugins/cash/refund_services.py exposes the read-only refund_coverage_for_cash(member, cash_transaction_ref) named read, and pmo_plugins/settlement/clearance_services.py adds clearance_coverage_for_cash plus minimally changes create_clearance.remaining_cash and cash_candidates_for_open_item.available_cents to gross - active cleared - refunded - returned. Reason: PH-232's formula only subtracted active clearances, so refund-then-clearance could jointly exceed the posted gross; the symmetric formula makes both write paths use the same derived ceiling. Clearance semantics, events, amounts and all other PH-232 logic are unchanged.

Known PH-232 spec/implementation gap disclosed: the PH-232 spec's 'cash un-cleared balance = posted gross - sum(active cleared)' text predates refunds/returns. The implementation now subtracts active refunds/returns for joint coverage. PH-232 is already done, so its spec was not edited here; the Lead will register a small follow-up in the PH-247 planning slot to sync that wording.

The reverse cash produced by a refund/bank return is created through the PH-230 posting owner service, so it also carries the standard canonical cash.transaction_recorded.v1 event and cash_transaction.post receipt in addition to the refund/return canonical event. This keeps the existing 'every posted cash fact has exactly one recorded event and posting receipt' invariant intact; the refund/return event is additional provenance, not a replacement.

CashReceipt is reused for idempotency with action=refund / bank_return as the spec permits; the produced cash posting receipt gets a deterministic server-derived token (uuid5 of the produced cash id and label) so both receipts coexist under the org+token uniqueness rule.

The produced cash fact uses the original effective counterparty (transaction.counterparty_id or latest unreversed counterparty identify match) as payee; when no effective counterparty exists it is stored as unidentified with a refund/return label. The server generates the external_source_key (REFUND-/RETURN- + uuid4 hex); caller-supplied keys are not accepted.

Refund requires original direction=in; bank return accepts any posted original and reverses its direction. The new cash transaction_date equals refund_date/return_date, which therefore must be non-future, above locked_through and in an active, not-closed AccountingPeriod.

No public canonical cash.refund.record/v1 or cash.return.record/v1 channel is exposed; only private services implement them, and caller-supplied balances/proofs/posted fields are rejected by the strict argument signature.
Offset coverage is explicitly reserved on the cross-owner interfaces as offset_cents=0/offset_implemented=false rather than fabricated.
